paths.reason: Same-site, rate-limited checkout creation calls Stripe and depends on an approved release, Redis and payment metadata.
Payment-gated redirect exposes delivery only after order-state verification; delivery target and entitlement semantics need review.
Order status is browser-nonce scoped and backed by Redis/Stripe; no deployed-state assertion is available.
Presentation makes receipt and Drive-delivery assertions that require product, terms and fulfillment approval.
Styles are coupled exclusively to deferred digital shop routes.
Starts route checkout or follows legacy hosted links; no legacy link is evidence of payment or delivery.
Claims payment confirmation and delivery access, requiring end-to-end product acceptance.
Receipt route is inseparable from the deferred order contract.
All releases have approvedAt null; source is intentionally fail-closed, not active delivery authority.
Uses Stripe secret and Redis plus live payment-link/price verification; values and provider health were not inspected.
Defines payment/order validation and delivery approval contract for the deferred flow.
Defines products, legacy hosted links and delivery hold; cannot establish active products or terms from source bytes.
Origin allowlist is security-critical shared checkout infrastructure and must be adopted with its callers.
Bounded anonymous event route needs current rate/origin compatibility verification.
CRON_SECRET-protected reporting must remain unavailable without configured authorization.
Minute aggregate report has Redis and CRON dependency.
Fixed-destination redirect and best-effort aggregate measurement require approved experiment policy.
User notice must be checked against the finally approved collection and retention behavior.
Local opt-out and PostHog opt-out must be mounted with the selected global initializer.
Single route event bridge is safe only after duplicate Pages/App Router initialization is removed.
Preserves DNT/GPC/local opt-out boundary; event allowlist must be reconciled with active callers.
Anonymous visitor/session storage and batching require consent-surface alignment.
Redis aggregate retention and capacity behavior require storage key/retention assessment.
Bounded event schema is a privacy boundary and must remain source-owned, not widened by callers.
Uses aggregate Redis counts with 35-day retention; provider availability is unverified.
Fixed experiments and destinations need owner confirmation before public use.

conflicts.reason: Recovery footer preserves privacy discoverability; production metadata has historical fixed 350 count and no technical gain.
Recovery checkoutHold prevents unverified purchase guidance; digital buttons await deferred M1.
Recovery copy avoids unsupported exclusivity, sales-use and allocation claims.
Replace raw PostHog initializer only as part of approved M2 so DNT/GPC/local opt-out and exactly-once router mounts hold.
Recovery derives from R7-A canonical projection and returns UNKNOWN; production fixed 359/225/134 fallback is rejected.
Recovery fixes ByteString-safe title and retains current provider/model/timeout policy; no provider availability or routing policy is inferred.
Route events through privacy-safe M2 boundary only; do not make collection a condition of user functionality.
Retains checkout holds and avoids production delivery/availability/license promises; does not invent a Chat product.
Use M2 shared bridge rather than raw dynamic PostHog init; eliminate App/Pages duplication.
